vpn/services/gatus/config/config.yaml carries live credentials in plaintext, including SSH private-key blocks. Never grep it with a context flag (-A/-B), and never print a parsed form of it - json.dumps of a single endpoint dict renders the key field verbatim. Read the KEY NAMES only; to compare a value, hash it in place. The read discipline is necessary but not sufficient: the PRINT is the second chokepoint, and it is the one that fails when the read felt safe. A third chokepoint is any TOOL whose output path renders the file's content: a diff, a checksum-and-dump, or a guard that prints a drift diff between two key-bearing copies discloses both. Read the output path before you ship the tool, not after.

announcements.text: infra_mac-cdp-tunnel (endpoint_id 15) was RED for 20 h 18 min: Gatus's own event table reads UNHEALTHY 2026-10-23T10:05:09Z -> HEALTHY 2026-10-24T06:23:09Z, and every probe in that window failed. An earlier version of this entry read '110 results / 0 failures', which was true only of the window it was read in, four hours before the outage began. THE MECHANISM, read from the endpoint's own definition rather than inferred: it is NOT a Mac-localhost check. The URL is ssh://78.17.187.4:15259 — which `getent hosts` resolves to THIS host, agents — and the body then runs `curl -s --max-time 3 http://localhost:9222/json/version | grep -c Macintosh` ON AGENTS. `grep -c` exits 1 on zero matches, so the probe is red whenever nothing listens on agents' loopback:9222; the probed object is the FORWARDER, not the Mac. THE MAC WAS HEALTHY THROUGHOUT: with the endpoint red, `ssh mac` succeeded and CDP answered Chrome/150.0.7871.1016 with a Macintosh User-Agent. THE DEFECT WAS SUPERVISION, NOW CLOSED. The forwarder was hand-launched every time, so it died and nothing brought it back. It is now a repo unit, agents/services/mac-cdp/mac-cdp-tunnel.service (vds-servers 6bd06c02), Restart=always with ServerAliveInterval 15 x3 — so ssh EXITS on a missed probe when the Mac sleeps instead of holding a half-open socket that reads up while forwarding nothing. Supervision is proven by positive control, not asserted: the MainPID was killed deliberately, systemd restarted it, NRestarts went 0 -> 1, the listener returned and the predicate read green. It binds BOTH loopbacks because `getent hosts localhost` on agents returns ::1 only, so an IPv4-only bind would pass solely through curl's fallback. THE MONTH IS WORSE THAN ANY RETAINED WINDOW SHOWS: endpoint 15 is 6,151 successful of 42,355 executions = 85.48% failure, and endpoint 13 (mac-tunnel) is 3,135 of 8,476 = 63.01% failure, so 13 reading 109/109 today describes the last ~1.8 h and not the month. Anything longer than the retained window reads endpoint_uptimes.
announcements.evidence: Read 2026-10-24T06:23Z-06:54:27Z. Gatus on vpn, sqlite file:/data/projects/gatus/data/gatus.db?mode=ro. endpoint_events for endpoint_id 15, latest six by endpoint_event_id desc: HEALTHY 2026-10-24T06:23:09, UNHEALTHY 2026-10-23T10:05:09, HEALTHY 2026-10-22T22:01:56, UNHEALTHY 2026-10-22T22:00:59, HEALTHY 2026-10-22T16:26:56, UNHEALTHY 2026-10-22T13:48:56 — the 10-23T10:05:09 -> 10-24T06:23:09 episode is 20 h 18 min. endpoint_results ep15 retained window: 108 results, 32 successful, oldest 2026-10-24T05:07:09, newest 06:54:09, last success 06:54:09. ep13: 109 results / 109 successful, newest 06:52:08. endpoint_uptimes 30-day, 85 entries each: ep15 42,355 executions / 6,151 successful = 85.48% failure; ep13 8,476 / 3,135 = 63.01% failure. Endpoint definitions from the deployed config, structure only: mac-cdp-tunnel url ssh://78.17.187.4:15259 interval 1m body 'curl -s --max-time 3 http://localhost:9222/json/version | grep -c Macintosh' conditions '[CONNECTED] == true' and '[STATUS] == 0'; agents url ssh://78.17.187.4:15259 interval 5m body '/usr/local/bin/host-diag' — the SAME URL, differing only in body and cadence, which is why one stayed green while the other went red. agents' ~/.ssh/config maps 'Host agents' to 127.0.0.1:22 and vpn's maps it to 78.17.187.4:15259; `getent hosts localhost` on agents returns ::1 only. Forwarder before the fix: absent (no :9222 listener; the only surviving `ssh -L` was an unrelated 15432->apps tunnel). Mac verified healthy 2026-10-24T06:20Z: ssh mac returned SSH_OK and curl http://localhost:9222/json/version returned Chrome/150.0.7871.1016 with a Macintosh User-Agent. Fix: agents/services/mac-cdp/mac-cdp-tunnel.service, vds-servers commit 6bd06c02, ledger n=1740 claim / n=1741 run. The prior text's '110 results / 0 failures (newest 2026-10-23T06:54:15Z)' was true only of the window it was read in, four hours before the outage began.

announcements.text: THE HAZARD IS NO LONGER HYPOTHETICAL: the kernel OOM-killed this daemon at 2026-10-24T06:06:44Z. systemd's own record reads 'A process of this unit has been killed by the OOM killer' then 'Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL', and dmesg carries oom-kill:constraint=CONSTRAINT_MEMCG with oom_memcg=/user.slice/user-0.slice/user@0.service/app.slice/opencrabs-ops.service, task=opencrabs, pid=3237387, oom_score_adj=100 — pid 3237387 being the very process the previous text called the live MainPID. The unit restarted at 06:06:50Z (MainPID 701185, NRestarts 4). Live at 2026-10-24T06:34:53Z, 28 minutes after that restart, the new incarnation is ALREADY at memory.current 2,111,193,088 of 2,147,483,648 B = 98.31% (headroom 34.6 MiB), swap.current 1,757,540,352 of 2,684,354,560 = 65.47%, memory.peak 143,360 B OVER memory.max, memory.events high 0 / max 69,301 / oom 0 / oom_kill 0 — and that zero is the PER-INCARNATION counter: it reads 0 because the kill it should have counted happened to the PREVIOUS incarnation, so a fresh zero is not evidence of a clean life. The same host also OOM-killed the FAMILY profile daemon (opencrabs.service, pid 4086328) at 2026-10-23T10:21:25Z, so this is a host-pressure pattern, not one unit's bad luck. WHAT STILL HOLDS: the watcher exists (infra_oc-ops-daemon, endpoint_id 34, pushing false on restart and a true heartbeat every 600 s); THE RESERVE IS ONE REMAINDER, not the swap line — the kill predicate is current + swap.current >= max + swap.max, so headroom and swap-free are two distributions of a single number, sampled five times at 12 s intervals on 2026-10-23 reading 103 / 67 / 110 / 241 / 102 MiB; and quote no single-instant burst/remainder ratio, because the same pair reads 2.47x, 4.87x or 15.9x depending only on which sample is chosen. Raising the cap is NOT a free option: Committed_AS exceeded CommitLimit by 439 MiB at the 2026-10-23T06:52:36Z read, and that gap itself moves fast, so carry the sign and not the magnitude. TWO MEASUREMENT TRAPS WILL MAKE THIS ENTRY LOOK FALSE. It describes a USER unit, so a bare `systemctl show opencrabs-ops.service` (system scope) answers MainPID=0, MemoryMax=infinity, ActiveState=inactive -- fabricated defaults for a unit that does not exist at that scope; only `systemctl --user` answers, and it returns the cap. And `dmesg -T` reads 24 s AHEAD of the journal on this host (06:07:08 against 06:06:44 for the same kill) because it converts from monotonic with the current offset, so it is the wrong instrument for an instant. dmesg's ops-unit kill count is a RING-BUFFER WINDOW, not a lifetime total.

announcements.text: The two board/ledger agreement gates are RETIRED, not red. tests/test_close_board_recorded.py and tests/test_board_intake_recorded.py assert a board/ledger close agreement, and this factory's issue board IS its ledger — ONE surface — so the two-surface predicate is INAPPLICABLE rather than failed. They were declared RED BY DESIGN at ledger n=611 and were the only REDs in the 23-gate audit. As of 2026-10-19 they are retired through the KIT'S DECLARED-ABSENT STATE, never by deletion: each reads the declared boundary from docs/ledger-invariants.json, this tree declares none, so each prints a named SKIP ('no docs/ledger-invariants.json — the boundary is a DECLARED factory parameter (#78 clause b)') and STILL RUNS EVERY PROBE — 11 on the close gate, 15 on the intake gate. HOW TO READ THEM NOW: a SKIP is the expected, correct state and is NOT a regression; but a RED from either gate IS a real defect — the retire was built so it cannot disguise a removed or broken gate. The four judgement probes are hermetic (a synthetic tree), and each gate keeps a positive control: a DECLARED boundary must still fail a bad row. The old 'RED BY DESIGN, do not file as a regression' instruction is WITHDRAWN — filing one of these as a regression is now the wrong call only if it SKIPPED; if it FAILED, file it. Owner directive 2026-10-19: 'i don't want to be asked such low level questions any more' — q27 is answered and the class (kit convention, internal mechanics) is now HQ's to decide, never the owner register's. Commits aed7c5af (gates + roles/hq.md + ledger n=1482) and 0c4952eb (prose refs). Full audit after: 24/24 gates PASS.

announcements.text: The cgroup that carries this factory's work on agents - opencrabs-ops.service - has a HARD MEMORY CAP and NO CPU CEILING. cgroup.controllers reads 'memory pids' and the parent app.slice/cgroup.subtree_control reads the same, so the cpu controller is never delegated and cpu.max does not EXIST there. The controller is not missing from the host: app.slice/cgroup.controllers reads 'cpu memory pids', so cpu is AVAILABLE one level up and a '+cpu' write at that parent is the only route - no unit-level edit can produce a ceiling; 'empty' and 'absent' are different artifacts and only the second is true. Measured 2026-10-23T07:08:45Z-07:09:34Z: two windows (15 s and 20 s) read busy 98.38% / 99.01% with idle 1.62% / 0.99%, and host-diag's own run at 07:09:43Z returned '1042 87 1315' rc=1 - load15 10.42 against LOAD_MAX 10.00, disk 87% and MemAvailable 1315 MB both INSIDE their thresholds (DISK_MAX 90, MEM_MIN_MB 80), so the load leg is the SOLE trigger. load15 sits between the p99 (8.63) and the 5-day max (12.99) of its own ldavg-15 calibration, and it was FALLING across this pass: 11.52 at 07:05:17Z -> 10.42 at 07:09:43Z while load1 went 9.09 -> 7.25. THE LOAD IS THE FACTORY'S OWN WORK: the top consumers at the sample were two node render.mjs at 125% and 121% CPU, an audit.py gate at 101%, and two pytest suites - concurrent gate runs, registry renders and test suites from several lanes, not a host fault and not an outside tenant. TWO THINGS THAT DO NOT HOLD. (1) 'The alert cannot clear quickly' is correct and is NOT a stuck probe - load15 is a 15-minute EWMA, which is why load1 had already fallen to 7.25 while load15 still read 10.42. (2) 'Steal is small, so the CPU is the host's own' is NOT established: the two windows read steal 11.35% and 23.54% (with iowait 14.75% in the second) against a 6.83% lifetime average, sar at the host's own 600 s resolution read 6.20% / 8.53% / 10.25% at 07:00 / 07:10 / 07:20, and an 8 s delta at 07:23:40Z read 9.91% (323 of 3260 jiffies) - so steal rises and falls WITH this factory's own load, which makes it a second cause alongside our work and not a substitute for it. The asymmetry is the durable fact: on the same 4-core box the memory side is bounded (2 GiB + 2.5 GiB swap, remainder sampled 67 MiB at 06:53:41Z and 551-678 MiB at 07:08-07:09Z) and the CPU side is bounded by nothing.
